seoTitle: Share Your TradingView Chart as Image, Link, or Tweet
metaDescription: Learn how to use TradingView's camera icon to download a chart image, copy it to your clipboard, share a link, or tweet it directly.
intro: A trade setup is only useful to other people if you can actually get it out of your own workspace, and TradingView bundles every way to do that behind a single camera icon in the chart toolbar. From there you can grab a downloadable image, copy the chart straight to your clipboard, generate a live link that mirrors your exact indicators and drawings, or post it to Twitter without leaving the page. This guide follows that flow on a real Dow Jones chart, from the toolbar icon through to what the shared, published version actually looks like on the other end.

steps.heading: Open the chart you want to share
steps.body: Pull up the chart with your setup on it — indicators, trendlines, watchlist, whatever you want the recipient to see included. In this example it's a Dow Jones Industrial Average (US30) chart on CAPITALCOM with a 9-period EMA and SMA plotted, inside a workspace named "Idle For Testing." Whatever is currently drawn and visible on the chart is what gets captured in the snapshot, so it's worth tidying up any stray drawings before you go further.

image.caption: The chart set up and ready to share, with its indicators and watchlist visible exactly as they'll appear in the snapshot.

steps.heading: Find the camera icon in the toolbar
steps.body: Look at the row of icons above the chart, next to the workspace name and Save link — you'll see a magnifying glass, a hexagon-shaped settings icon, a fullscreen icon, and a camera icon at the far right. That camera icon is the entry point for every sharing option TradingView offers; nothing about sharing lives in the main left-hand drawing toolbar or the symbol search bar.

image.caption: The toolbar above the chart, with the camera icon on the right that opens every sharing and snapshot option.

steps.heading: Open the Chart Snapshot menu
steps.body: Click the camera icon and a Chart Snapshot panel drops down with five options stacked vertically: Download image, Copy image, Copy link, Open in new tab, and Tweet image. Each one does something slightly different with the same underlying snapshot, so the choice comes down to where you actually want the chart to end up — a saved file, your clipboard, a URL, or straight to a tweet.

image.caption: The Chart Snapshot menu, listing Download image, Copy image, Copy link, and Open in new tab as the ways to export the current chart.

steps.heading: Download or copy the image directly
steps.body: Choose Download image if you want a saved picture file on your device — useful for attaching to an email, dropping into a presentation, or uploading manually to a platform that doesn't accept pasted images. Choose Copy image instead if you'd rather skip the file entirely and paste the chart directly into a chat app, document, or forum post that supports pasting from the clipboard.

steps.heading: Copy a link to the live chart
steps.body: Selecting Copy link or Open in new tab generates a published, view-only version of your chart hosted on TradingView's own domain, complete with a "created with TradingView.com" header, the timestamp it was generated, and a Copy link button of its own on that page. Anyone who opens the link sees the same indicators, price levels, and drawings you had on screen, in the same interactive format, rather than a flat image — which makes it the better option when you want someone to actually explore the chart rather than just glance at it.

image.caption: The published chart snapshot page generated from the share link, showing the creator's name, the creation timestamp, and its own Copy link button.

steps.heading: Tweet the chart if you're posting publicly
steps.body: If your goal is to post the setup publicly, the Tweet image option in the same Chart Snapshot menu takes the current chart, attaches it to a new tweet composer, and lets you add your own commentary before posting straight to Twitter/X. It saves the step of downloading the image and re-uploading it manually, which matters if you're sharing setups regularly and don't want the extra round trip every time.

faq.question: Where is the sharing option on TradingView?
faq.answer: Click the camera icon in the chart's top toolbar, next to the workspace name and Save link, to open the Chart Snapshot menu with every sharing option.

faq.question: Can I share a chart without downloading it?
faq.answer: Yes, the Copy image option in the Chart Snapshot menu copies the chart to your clipboard so you can paste it directly into a message or document without saving a file first.

faq.question: Can others view my chart as a live link?
faq.answer: Yes, Copy link or Open in new tab generates a published version of your chart hosted on TradingView.com, showing the same indicators and drawings in the same interactive format.

faq.question: Can I tweet my chart directly from TradingView?
faq.answer: Yes, the Tweet image option in the Chart Snapshot menu attaches your current chart to a new tweet you can post straight from TradingView.

faq.question: Does the shared link show who created the chart?
faq.answer: Yes, the published snapshot page includes a header naming the account that created it along with the exact date and time it was generated.
